**Analyzing the Duplicate Image Issue**

Alright, let's break this down. The core issue is that we're generating duplicate image files in storage. module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    class_methods do
      def has_markdown(name, strict_loading: strict_loading_by_default)
        class_eval <<-CODE, __FILE__, __LINE__ + 1
          def #{name}
            markdown_#{name} || build_markdown_#{name}
          end

          def #{name}?
            markdown_#{name}.present?
          end

          def #{name}=(content)
            self.#{name}.content = content
          end
        CODE

        has_one :"markdown_#{name}", -> { where(name: name) },
          class_name: "ActionText::Markdown", as: :record, inverse_of: :record, autosave: true, dependent: :destroy,
          strict_loading: strict_loading

        scope :"with_markdown_#{name}", -> { includes("markdown_#{name}") }
        scope :"with_markdown_#{name}_and_embeds", -> { includes("markdown_#{name}": { embeds_attachments: :blob }) }
      end
    end

    def safe_markdown_attribute(name)
      if self.class.reflect_on_association("markdown_#{name}")&.klass == ActionText::Markdown
        public_send(name)

    end
  end

class ActiveStorage::NamedVariant # :nodoc:
  attr_reader :transformations, :preprocessed

  def initialize(options)
    @preprocessed      = options[:preprocessed]

  def process(record)

    preprocessed?(record) ? :later : :lazily
  end

  private
    def preprocessed?(record)
      case preprocessed
      when Symbol

      when Proc

require "active_support/core_ext/module/delegation"

# = Active Storage \Attachment
#
# Attachments associate records with blobs. Usually that's a one record-many blobs relationship,
# but it is possible to associate many different records with the same blob. A foreign-key constraint
# on the attachments table prevents blobs from being purged if they’re still attached to any records.
#
# Attachments also have access to all methods from ActiveStorage::Blob.
#
# If you wish to preload attachments or blobs, you can use these scopes:
#
#   # preloads attachments, their corresponding blobs, and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.all.with_attached_avatars
#
#   # preloads blobs and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
class ActiveStorage::Attachment < ActiveStorage::Record
  define_model_callbacks :upload

  after_upload :mirror_blob_later
  after_upload :analyze_blob_later
  after_upload :create_variants

  # Set to true when immediate variants have been processed from local io,
  # so create_variants knows to skip them.
  attr_accessor :immediate_variants_processed

  # Set to true for fresh uploads (io provided), false for existing blobs.
  # Used to determine whether to run :upload callbacks in after_create_commit.
  attr_accessor :pending_upload

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated record.
  belongs_to :record, polymorphic: true, touch: ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated ActiveStorage::Blob.
  belongs_to :blob, class_name: "ActiveStorage::Blob", autosave: true, inverse_of: :attachments

  delegate_missing_to :blob
  delegate :signed_id, to: :blob

  after_create_commit :run_upload_callbacks, unless: :pending_upload
  after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later

  ##
  # :singleton-method:
  #
  # Eager load all variant records on an attachment at once.
  #
  #   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
  scope :with_all_variant_records, -> { includes(blob: {
    variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob },
    preview_image_attachment: { blob: { variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob } } }
  }) }

  # Called by Attached::Changes::CreateOne to handle the upload workflow for
  # fresh uploads. Processes immediate variants and analyzes from the local io
  # (avoiding a download round-trip), uploads the blob, then runs the :upload
  # callbacks.
  #
  # For existing blob attachments, the :upload callbacks are run via
  # after_create_commit instead.
  def uploaded(io:)
    blob.local_io = io

    process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
    analyze_blob_from_io(io)

    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    blob.upload_without_unfurling(io)

    # Persist analysis metadata if the blob was already saved (happens when
    # upload runs in after_commit, after the blob was saved via autosave).
    blob.save! if blob.persisted? && blob.metadata_changed?

    run_upload_callbacks
  ensure
    blob.local_io = nil
  end

  # Synchronously deletes the attachment and {purges the blob}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge].
  def purge
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge
  end

  # Deletes the attachment and {enqueues a background job}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge_later] to purge the blob.
  def purge_later
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge_later
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Proxy files through application. This avoids having a redirect and makes files easier to cache.
#
# WARNING: All Active Storage controllers are publicly accessible by default. The
# generated URLs are hard to guess, but permanent by design. If your files
# require a higher level of protection consider implementing
# {Authenticated Controllers}[https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#authenticated-controllers].
class ActiveStorage::Representations::ProxyController < ActiveStorage::Representations::BaseController
  include ActiveStorage::Streaming
  include ActiveStorage::DisableSession

  def show
    http_cache_forever public: true do
      send_blob_stream @representation, disposition: params[:disposition]
    end
  end
end

class ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob < ActiveStorage::BaseJob
  queue_as { ActiveStorage.queues[:transform] }

  discard_on ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
  retry_on ActiveStorage::IntegrityError, attempts: 10, wait: :polynomially_longer

  def perform(blob, variants:, process:)
    @blob = blob
    @process = process

    create_preview_image if preview_image_needed?

    variants.each do |transformations|
      ActiveStorage::TransformJob.public_send(perform_method, @blob, transformations)
    end
  end

  private
    def create_preview_image
      @blob.preview({}).processed
    end

    def preview_image_needed?
      @blob.previewable? && !@blob.preview_image.attached?
    end

    def perform_method
      (@process == :immediately) ? :perform_now : :perform_later
    end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "marcel"

# = Active Storage \Variation
#
# A set of transformations that can be applied to a blob to create a variant. This class is exposed via
# the ActiveStorage::Blob#variant method and should rarely be used directly.
#
# In case you do need to use this directly, it's instantiated using a hash of transformations where
# the key is the command and the value is the arguments. Example:
#
#   ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [100, 100], colourspace: "b-w", rotate: "-90", saver: { trim: true })
#
# The options map directly to {ImageProcessing}[https://github.com/janko/image_processing] commands.
class ActiveStorage::Variation
  attr_reader :transformations

  class << self
    # Returns a Variation instance based on the given variator. If the variator is a Variation, it is
    # returned unmodified. If it is a String, it is passed to ActiveStorage::Variation.decode. Otherwise,
    # it is assumed to be a transformations Hash and is passed directly to the constructor.
    def wrap(variator)
      case variator
      when self
        variator
      when String
        decode variator
      else
        new variator
      end
    end

    # Returns a Variation instance with the transformations that were encoded by +encode+.
    def decode(key)
      new ActiveStorage.verifier.verify(key, purpose: :variation)
    end

    # Returns a signed key for the +transformations+, which can be used to refer to a specific
    # variation in a URL or combined key (like <tt>ActiveStorage::Variant#key</tt>).
    def encode(transformations)
      ActiveStorage.verifier.generate(transformations, purpose: :variation)
    end
  end

  def initialize(transformations)
    @transformations = transformations.deep_symbolize_keys
  end

  def default_to(defaults)
    self.class.new transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)
  end

  # Accepts a File object, performs the +transformations+ against it, and
  # saves the transformed image into a temporary file.
  def transform(file, &block)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("transform.active_storage") do
      transformer.transform(file, format: format, &block)
    end
  end

  def format
    transformations.fetch(:format, :png).tap do |format|
      if Marcel::Magic.by_extension(format.to_s).nil?
        raise ArgumentError, "Invalid variant format (#{format.inspect})"
      end
    end
  end

  def content_type
    Marcel::MimeType.for(extension: format.to_s)
  end

  # Returns a signed key for all the +transformations+ that this variation was instantiated with.
  def key
    self.class.encode(transformations)
  end

  def digest
    OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.base64digest Marshal.dump(transformations)
  end

  private
    def transformer
      ActiveStorage.variant_transformer.new(transformations.except(:format))
    end
end

# = Active Storage \Variant With Record
#
# Like an ActiveStorage::Variant, but keeps detail about the variant in the database as an
# ActiveStorage::VariantRecord. This is used if +ActiveStorage.track_variants+ is enabled.
class ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord
  include ActiveStorage::Blob::Servable

  attr_reader :blob, :variation

  delegate :content_type, to: :variation

  def initialize(blob, variation)
    @blob, @variation = blob, ActiveStorage::Variation.wrap(variation)
  end

  def processed

    self
  end

    record&.image
  end

  def filename
    ActiveStorage::Filename.new "#{blob.filename.base}.#{variation.format.downcase}"
  end

  # Destroys record and deletes file from service.
  def destroy
    record&.destroy
  end

  delegate :key, :url, :download, to: :image, allow_nil: true

  # Returns true if the variant has already been processed and stored.

    record.present?

  # Process the variant from a local io, avoiding a download from the service.
  # This is an optimization for when the original file is still available locally
  # (e.g., during the initial upload flow).
  def process_from_io(io) # :nodoc:

      create_or_find_record(image: {

require "marcel"

# = Active Storage \Variation
#
# A set of transformations that can be applied to a blob to create a variant. This class is exposed via
# the ActiveStorage::Blob#variant method and should rarely be used directly.
#
# In case you do need to use this directly, it's instantiated using a hash of transformations where
# the key is the command and the value is the arguments. Example:
#
#   ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [100, 100], colourspace: "b-w", rotate: "-90", saver: { trim: true })
#
# The options map directly to {ImageProcessing}[https://github.com/janko/image_processing] commands.
class ActiveStorage::Variation
  attr_reader :transformations

  class << self
    # Returns a Variation instance based on the given variator. If the variator is a Variation, it is
    # returned unmodified. If it is a String, it is passed to ActiveStorage::Variation.decode. Otherwise,
    # it is assumed to be a transformations Hash and is passed directly to the constructor.
    def wrap(variator)
      case variator
      when self
        variator
      when String
        decode variator
      else
        new variator
      end
    end

    # Returns a Variation instance with the transformations that were encoded by +encode+.
    def decode(key)
      new ActiveStorage.verifier.verify(key, purpose: :variation)
    end

    # Returns a signed key for the +transformations+, which can be used to refer to a specific
    # variation in a URL or combined key (like <tt>ActiveStorage::Variant#key</tt>).
    def encode(transformations)
      ActiveStorage.verifier.generate(transformations, purpose: :variation)
    end
  end

  def initialize(transformations)
    @transformations = transformations.deep_symbolize_keys
  end

  def default_to(defaults)
    self.class.new transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)
  end

  # Accepts a File object, performs the +transformations+ against it, and
  # saves the transformed image into a temporary file.
  def transform(file, &block)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("transform.active_storage") do
      transformer.transform(file, format: format, &block)
    end
  end

  def format
    transformations.fetch(:format, :png).tap do |format|
      if Marcel::Magic.by_extension(format.to_s).nil?
        raise ArgumentError, "Invalid variant format (#{format.inspect})"
      end
    end
  end

    Marcel::MimeType.for(extension: format.to_s)
  end

  def key
    self.class.encode(transformations)
  end

  def digest
    OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.base64digest Marshal.dump(transformations)
  end

  private
    def transformer
      ActiveStorage.variant_transformer.new(transformations.except(:format))

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :ensure_index_is_not_empty, only: :index
  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]
  before_action :set_users, only: %i[ new edit ]
  before_action :ensure_editable, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @books = Book.accessable_or_published.ordered
  end

  def new
    @book = Book.new
  end

  def create
    book = Book.create! book_params
    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.update(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable
      head :forbidden unless @book.editable?
    end

    def ensure_index_is_not_empty
      if !signed_in? && Book.published.none?
        require_authentication
      end
    end

    def book_params
      params.require(:book).permit(:title, :subtitle, :author, :cover, :remove_cover, :everyone_access, :theme)
    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)
    end

    def remove_cover
      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

require_relative "test/test_helper"

class ReproTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  test "reproduce duplicate picture variant on upload + background job + reader fetch" do
    book = books(:handbook)

    transforms = []
    subscriber = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") do |*args|
      transforms << args
    end

    # Upload a JPEG photograph (and also check webp)
    jpg_path = Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg")
    uploaded_file = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(jpg_path, "image/jpeg")

    blobs_before = ActiveStorage::Blob.count
    variants_before = ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.count
    storage_files_before = Dir.glob(File.join(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root, "**", "*")).select { |f| File.file?(f) }

    puts "Before upload: blobs=#{blobs_before}, variant_records=#{variants_before}, storage_files=#{storage_files_before.size}"

    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
        leaf: { title: "My Photo" },
        picture: { image: uploaded_file, caption: "A photo" }
      }
      assert_response :success
    end

    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    picture = leaf.picture
    blob = picture.image.blob

    storage_files_after_bg = Dir.glob(File.join(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root, "**", "*")).select { |f| File.file?(f) }
    puts "After upload + background jobs:"
    puts "  transforms count: #{transforms.size}"
    puts "  blob variant_records count: #{blob.variant_records.count}"
    puts "  blob variant_records digests: #{blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest).inspect}"
    puts "  new storage files: #{storage_files_after_bg.size - storage_files_before.size}"

    # Now reader opens the book page
    transforms_before_read = transforms.size
    get book_slug_path(book)
    assert_response :success

    # Find the picture img src on the book page
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)
    img = doc.at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} img")
    img_src = img["src"]
    puts "Book page img src: #{img_src}"

    # Reader fetches the picture URL it links to
    get img_src
    puts "GET img_src status: #{response.status}, location: #{response.headers['Location']}"
    assert_response :redirect

    follow_redirect!
    puts "GET redirect status: #{response.status}, content_type: #{response.content_type}, bytes: #{response.body.bytesize}"
    assert_response :success
    reader_bytes_digest = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(response.body)

    storage_files_after_read = Dir.glob(File.join(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root, "**", "*")).select { |f| File.file?(f) }
    puts "After reader opens book page and fetches picture:"
    puts "  transforms during read: #{transforms.size - transforms_before_read}"
    puts "  total transforms: #{transforms.size}"
    puts "  blob variant_records count: #{blob.variant_records.reload.count}"
    puts "  blob variant_records digests: #{blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest).inspect}"
    puts "  new storage files total: #{storage_files_after_read.size - storage_files_before.size}"
    puts "  reader bytes sha256: #{reader_bytes_digest}"

    # Also check opening the picture page itself

    get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
    assert_response :success
    leaf_doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)

  ensure

  end
end

messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Variant Digest Discrepancies**

Okay, hold on a second! I need to stop everything and really examine these digests. Something crucial just jumped out at me. Let's compare the digests generated earlier during the `bin/rails runner` execution with the ones produced after the upload and background jobs, and then again when the reader accesses the book page.

Initially, we saw:

*   **v1.transformations:** `{resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: :webp}`
*   **v1.digest:** "YMihNeq9GahYwX+32EeyepYXE7Y="
*   **v2.transformations:** `{resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500], format: "webp"}`
*   **v2.digest:** "zt77FJ1GTgSdZvhW/wgYp2WAeRQ="

Now, after the upload process:

*   The number of transforms is 1.
*   The number of blob variant records is 1.
*   The variant records digests are: ["Li3Nbm42FApB65ORO8OkGZpNDOU="]

And then, when the reader opens the book page, the picture is fetched.  Here:

*   Transforms during read: 1.
*   Total transforms: 2.
*   The number of blob variant records is 2.
*   The variant records digests are: ["2iK4D6Pm4TeLcj8qTmXCQ2guK3c=", "Li3Nbm42FApB65ORO8OkGZpNDOU="]

Wait a minute, let's look at the Base64 payload embedded in the image URL!  Decoding that `eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2xpbWl0IjpbMTUwMCwxNTAwXX0sInB1ciI6InZhcmlhdGlvbiJ9fQ==` gives us `{"_rails":{"data":{"format":"webp","resize_to_limit":[1500,1500]},"pur":"variation"}}`!

I can see *two* immediately notable things:

1.  **Key Order:** The order of the keys in that hash is `format` *before* `resize_to_limit`. WHY? Because of the `default_to` and `transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)` logic, where `defaults` is `{ format: default_variant_format }`!  In Ruby, when merging two hashes with the same key, like `{ format: ... }.merge({ resize_to_limit: ..., format: ... })`, the first occurrence of the key in the merge ends up the one! It's because `reverse_merge` is `other_hash.merge(self)`!!
2.  **Symbol vs. String:** It's using `format: :webp` (a symbol) versus `format: "webp"` (a string)!

We need to now dig into these two digests: `"Li3Nbm42FApB65ORO8OkGZpNDOU="` and `"2iK4D6Pm4TeLcj8qTmXCQ2guK3c="`!!

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into ActiveStorage Variant Inconsistencies**

Okay, deep breath! Thank goodness we meticulously checked all the moving parts here. It's becoming clear why we're seeing these discrepancies, and it's a subtle but significant issue.

First, I had to confirm we understood the implications of ActiveStorage's internals.  Looking at those digests:

*   `Li3Nbm42FApB65ORO8OkGZpNDOU=` <= `{format: :webp, resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500]}`
*   `2iK4D6Pm4TeLcj8qTmXCQ2guK3c=` <= `{format: "webp", resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500]}`

It's evident the format's representation is the root cause. My primary focus became tracing how the `:format` symbol or string is handled throughout the variant generation process.

The `default_to` method looks like a key area of concern:
`default_to(defaults)` performs `transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)`. The important thing here is that the `defaults` includes `format: default_variant_format`. And since `reverse_merge` means the *`defaults`* always take precedence, the `:format` in there overwrites. That is one place where the :format can get updated.

`default_variant_format` then, is critical. If the image is a web image (png/jpeg/webp/gif), format is a string (e.g., `"jpg"`), or a symbol if the original image has no extension. If it's *not* a web image, the default is `:png` (a symbol), but *it's the format parameter* that is the source of the trouble.

Now, let's step through the specific example with `Picture`: We have the `large` variant defined with `format: :webp`.
*   We're using `process: :later`, and that means `ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob` serializes `:webp` with `ActiveJob::Serializers::SymbolSerializer` — *and that's important*, because the Symbol is preserved across serialization. It hits `ActiveStorage::TransformJob`, which runs `blob.variant(...)` which ultimately calls `Variation.wrap(...).default_to(...)` and the digest is properly built, as a symbol, resulting in `Li3Nbm42FApB65ORO8OkGZpNDOU=`.
*   However, when rendering the view, we do `image_tag @leaf.picture.large_image`. This calls `blob.variant()` *again*. The crucial step is the `rails_storage_redirect` helper. Because we're on 7.2 with `:json_allow_marshal` set for the serializer, the `:webp` symbol *is* converted to the string `"webp"` when generating the key. Then, when the browser hits the redirect, the `params[:variation_key]` contains the string `"webp"`. When that is parsed and run through the system again, and the key is verified, the internal keys are parsed and the string is used, resulting in the digest `2iK4D6Pm4TeLcj8qTmXCQ2guK3c=`!
*   The digest does *not* match, and the variant gets processed a *second* time.

So the core problem? The use of `:json_allow_marshal` in rails_storage_redirect converts the symbol to a string, resulting in an incompatible digest.

I need to confirm there aren't any other factors that could play into this, like double processing from attachment creation. I'll need to double check `ActiveStorage::Attachment#uploaded` and `after_create_commit` to confirm `create_variants` isn't called twice.

module ActiveStorage
  class Attached::Changes::CreateMany # :nodoc:
    attr_reader :name, :record, :attachables, :pending_uploads

    def initialize(name, record, attachables, pending_uploads: [])
      @name, @record, @attachables = name, record, Array(attachables)
      blobs.each(&:identify_without_saving)
      @pending_uploads = Array(pending_uploads) + subchanges_without_blobs
      attachments
    end

    def attachments
      @attachments ||= subchanges.collect(&:attachment)
    end

    def blobs
      @blobs ||= subchanges.collect(&:blob)
    end

    def analyze
      subchanges.each(&:analyze)
    end

    def upload
      pending_uploads.each(&:upload)
    end

    def save
      assign_associated_attachments
      reset_associated_blobs
    end

    private
      def subchanges
        @subchanges ||= attachables.collect { |attachable| build_subchange_from(attachable) }
      end

      def build_subchange_from(attachable)
        ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOneOfMany.new(name, record, attachable)
      end

      def subchanges_without_blobs
        subchanges.reject { |subchange| subchange.attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob) }
      end

      def assign_associated_attachments
        record.public_send("#{name}_attachments=", persisted_or_new_attachments)
      end

      def reset_associated_blobs
        record.public_send("#{name}_blobs").reset
      end

      def persisted_or_new_attachments
        attachments.select { |attachment| attachment.persisted? || attachment.new_record? }
      end
  end
end

module ActiveStorage
  class Attached::Changes::CreateMany # :nodoc:
    attr_reader :name, :record, :attachables, :pending_uploads

    def initialize(name, record, attachables, pending_uploads: [])
      @name, @record, @attachables = name, record, Array(attachables)
      blobs.each(&:identify_without_saving)
      @pending_uploads = Array(pending_uploads) + subchanges_without_blobs
      attachments
    end

    def attachments
      @attachments ||= subchanges.collect(&:attachment)
    end

    def blobs
      @blobs ||= subchanges.collect(&:blob)
    end

    def analyze
      subchanges.each(&:analyze)
    end

    def upload
      pending_uploads.each(&:upload)
    end

    def save
      assign_associated_attachments
      reset_associated_blobs
    end

    private
      def subchanges
        @subchanges ||= attachables.collect { |attachable| build_subchange_from(attachable) }
      end

      def build_subchange_from(attachable)
        ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOneOfMany.new(name, record, attachable)
      end

      def subchanges_without_blobs
        subchanges.reject { |subchange| subchange.attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob) }
      end

      def assign_associated_attachments
        record.public_send("#{name}_attachments=", persisted_or_new_attachments)
      end

      def reset_associated_blobs
        record.public_send("#{name}_blobs").reset
      end

      def persisted_or_new_attachments
        attachments.select { |attachment| attachment.persisted? || attachment.new_record? }
      end

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing and Resolving ActiveStorage Duplicate Variant Issue**

Okay, here's the situation as I understand it. I've been digging into this ActiveStorage issue with duplicate variants, and it's got my attention. It seems that Rails 7.1 introduced a subtle but significant change in how it handles serialized messages, specifically around `active_support.message_serializer`. Prior to 7.1, `:marshal` was the default, but it was switched to `:json_allow_marshal`. This matters because the `ActiveStorage::Variation#digest` method *still* relies on `Marshal.dump` to generate a unique key for image transformations, like resizing and format conversions.

The crux of the problem is that when you use a Symbol (like `:webp`) in your image processing transformations (e.g., in a Rails variant definition) and send this information through JSON serialization (which is what happens in the URL used to access the image), the Symbol becomes a String. Since `Marshal.dump` treats a Symbol and a String differently, we get different digests and, consequently, duplicate variants. This is exactly what the problem description is highlighting: An editor uploads a photograph, the background job runs and writes the derived copy — then the first reader to open the book triggers the same conversion again, and the second copy is kept next to the first forever.

So I need to ensure the solution satisfies all the prompt requirements: "Make an upload get derived once. After the background work has run, opening the book page and fetching the picture it links to does no image processing, and exactly one derived copy is in storage. What a reader is served does not change — the same picture they get today, byte for byte."

I've examined the code (line 308 of `railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb`) and also have been doing a systematic review to determine the best approach. Changing `config.active_support.message_serializer` to `:marshal` is a non-starter. It’s a security risk, it affects the entire application, and it could break existing functionality. It's too heavy-handed.

Changing `Picture#large_image` so it returns `variant.processed.image` or the variant's URL directly is also not the right solution, as it circumvents the expected behavior of variants and could lead to other issues, such as N+1 queries.

Monkey-patching `ActiveStorage::Variation` to ensure consistent serialization, for example, by forcing the transformations to convert the `:format` to a `"format"` string before being serialized, is also not a good approach. Why? It's a bit of a hack and may not be the most robust or future-proof solution.

It's clear that the solution that *does* work is to ensure that, when defining the `variant` in `Picture`, we use a string for the format. For example:
`attachable.variant :large, resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ], format: "webp", process: :later`

Using `"webp"` instead of `:webp` in the `format` option ensures that the transformations are serialized as a string from the very beginning. This consistency ensures that the digest generated by `Marshal.dump` matches across the background job, the URL key, and direct Ruby calls. This then prevents duplicate variants. In all the test cases I am reviewing, this ensures it's correct.

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)

            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end

**Analyzing the Impact of `webp` Format in ActiveStorage Variations**

Okay, so I'm facing this situation where everything seems to be byte-for-byte identical, content types match, and formats are downcased. And, it's working as expected, the `format: "webp"` is being served, which is great.

The big question now is, what's the best way to handle this: Change the `Picture` model alone, or patch `ActiveStorage::Variation`, or maybe both? I need to think this through very carefully.

Let's break down the options:

**Option 1: Modify `Picture` Model Only**

This involves updating the `Picture` model to specify the `format: "webp"` directly within the variant definition, like `attachable.variant :large, resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ], format: "webp", process: :later`.  This seems straightforward.

**Option 2: Patch `ActiveStorage::Variation` (or potentially modify both)**

This is where it gets trickier, and potentially riskier. I'd need to consider how to patch `ActiveStorage::Variation`. I could modify methods like `decode`, `encode`, `format`, or `digest`.

If I patch `ActiveStorage::Variation#digest`, like to normalize symbols to strings or use JSON serialization, I hit a potential major problem. If I change the `digest` method to use JSON instead of `Marshal.dump`, every existing `active_storage_variant_records.variation_digest` entry in the database will become invalid. That means every existing image will have to be reprocessed. That's a huge issue.

What if I normalize Symbol values to Strings in `Variation#initialize`? If I change `format: :webp` to `format: "webp"`, could it break other Vips/ImageProcessing options that *require* a symbol? I need to check.  Does `ImageProcessing::Vips` need symbols for options like `crop: :centre` or `saver: { subsample_mode: :on }`? I know that if the URL goes through JSON, the Vips process would already be getting strings, but does it matter? And here's another concern: monkey-patching Rails internals, especially when I'm using a Rails development version pinned to a specific GitHub commit, can be really fragile. If upstream Rails changes `ActiveStorage::Variation`, my patch could break.

And, if this is a solved problem in Rails (or even discussed), I need to find the related Rails commit or changelog to see what the core team did about it. I have to see, for example, why `ActiveStorage::Variation#digest` is still using `Marshal.dump` in the most recent version of Rails from the date I am seeing. That's important context.

So, I need to weigh the simplicity of the `Picture` model change against the potential risks of patching `ActiveStorage::Variation`, along with understanding the actual Rails context. I need to make sure I don't break existing images and that any patch is as robust as possible.

require "test_helper"

class BaselineTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  test "record baseline served bytes and variation keys" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    samples = [
      ["app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg", "image/jpeg"],
      ["app/assets/images/demo/fullscreen-IbQnfM.png", "image/png"],
      ["test/fixtures/files/reading.webp", "image/webp"],
      ["app/assets/images/demo/autosave-Ssql4X.gif", "image/gif"],
    ]

    samples.each do |relpath, ct|
      transforms = []
      sub = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") { |*a| transforms << a }

      uploaded = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(Rails.root.join(relpath), ct)
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
          leaf: { title: File.basename(relpath) },
          picture: { image: uploaded }
        }
        assert_response :success
      end

      leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
      bg_transforms = transforms.size

      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]
      variation_key = img_src.split("/")[-2]

      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success

      read_transforms = transforms.size - bg_transforms
      sha = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(response.body)
      blob = leaf.picture.image.blob

      puts "#{File.basename(relpath)} | ct=#{response.content_type} | bytes=#{response.body.bytesize} | sha256=#{sha} | bg_xforms=#{bg_transforms} | read_xforms=#{read_transforms} | variants=#{blob.variant_records.count} | vkey=#{variation_key}"
      ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(sub)
    end
  end
end
EOF

**Analyzing Image Processing Optimization**

Okay, here's what I'm seeing. The core optimization is clear: we've eliminated redundant image transformations. Looking at this before-and-after data, I'm struck by the consistency: identical SHA256 hashes confirm bit-level equivalence. The `read_xforms` flag has dropped from 1 to 0 across the board, and the `variants` count has shrunk from 2 to 1. The total storage files are down from 3 to 2, which seems right, one original and one derived copy. That indicates, at least for these examples, the system is correctly identifying and serving the optimized version.

Now, the real test is the edge cases. We need to ensure this optimization holds up under all sorts of scenarios. I'm thinking about the standard UI flow for picture creation and upload, the different user roles (editor, reader, unauthenticated), and the timing of background jobs. Updating pictures with new photos, or *just* the caption... those are crucial. I have to think of all scenarios. It's important to make sure the reverse order scenario is considered - readers fetching picture URLs *before* the background jobs are processed. Then, of course, direct uploads, ActiveStorage integration, TIFF files, and large images (scaling them properly is important), BMP images (since it's a fixed-pixel format), and finally, simulating Resque JSON serialization. To top it off, we have to make sure the same image representation URL is used across the different pages (leafable page, edit page, and book page).

I'm starting to write out all these edge cases, right, in a script. `/tmp/edge_cases.rb`, I'll start with that. It'll give me a solid way to test the system in a systematic way.

require "test_helper"

class EdgeCasesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  def count_transforms
    count = 0
    sub = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") { count += 1 }
    yield
    count
  ensure
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(sub)
  end

  def storage_file_count
    Dir.glob(File.join(ActiveStorage::Blob.service.root, "**", "*")).count { |f| File.file?(f) }
  end

  test "editor creates blank picture page, uploads photo via edit, bg job runs, unauthenticated reader opens published book and fetches image" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    book.update!(published: true)

    # Step 1: Editor clicks "+ Add a new picture page" (empty picture)
    post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream)
    assert_response :success
    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last

    files_before = storage_file_count

    # Step 2: Editor uploads photograph via update
    bg_transforms = count_transforms do
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        put leafable_path(leaf), params: {
          leaf: { title: "Uploaded Photo" },
          picture: {
            image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg"), "image/jpeg"),
            caption: "Nice photo"
          }
        }
        assert_response :no_content
      end
    end

    leaf.reload
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob
    assert_equal 1, bg_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.count
    assert_equal files_before + 2, storage_file_count # original + 1 derived

    # Step 3: Unauthenticated reader opens book page and fetches image
    sign_out
    read_transforms = count_transforms do
      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]

      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
      assert_equal "image/webp", response.content_type

      # Also open the picture leaf page itself and fetch its image
      get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
      assert_response :success
      leaf_img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("figure img")["src"]
      assert_equal img_src, leaf_img_src

      get leaf_img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
    end

    assert_equal 0, read_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count
    assert_equal files_before + 2, storage_file_count
  end

  test "reverse order: reader opens book and fetches picture BEFORE background job runs" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    files_before = storage_file_count

    post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
      leaf: { title: "Early Read" },
      picture: { image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg"), "image/jpeg") }
    }
    assert_response :success
    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob

    # Reader fetches BEFORE background job runs
    read_transforms = count_transforms do
      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]
      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
    end

    assert_equal 1, read_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count

    # Now background jobs run
    bg_transforms = count_transforms do
      perform_enqueued_jobs
    end

    assert_equal 0, bg_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count
    assert_equal files_before + 2, storage_file_count
  end

  test "editing caption after 10 minutes duplicates leafable with same blob and does zero re-processing" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
        leaf: { title: "Caption Test" },
        picture: { image: fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp") }
      }
    end

    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.count

    travel 20.minutes do
      caption_transforms = count_transforms do
        perform_enqueued_jobs do
          put leafable_path(leaf), params: { picture: { caption: "Updated caption" } }
          assert_response :no_content
        end
      end

      assert_equal 0, caption_transforms
      assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count
    end
  end

  test "oversized image (> 1500px) and TIFF (non-web image) both derive once" do
    book = books(:handbook)

    # Create a 2000x1600 TIFF image using Vips
    tiff_file = Tempfile.new(["big", ".tiff"])
    Vips::Image.black(2000, 1600, bands: 3).write_to_file(tiff_file.path)

    files_before = storage_file_count
    bg_transforms = count_transforms do
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
          leaf: { title: "Big TIFF" },
          picture: { image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(tiff_file.path, "image/tiff", true, original_filename: "big.tiff") }
        }
        assert_response :success
      end
    end

    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob
    assert_equal 1, bg_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.count
    assert_equal files_before + 2, storage_file_count

    read_transforms = count_transforms do
      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]
      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
      assert_equal "image/webp", response.content_type

      # Verify it actually resized to <= 1500x1500
      result_img = Vips::Image.new_from_buffer(response.body, "")
      assert_equal 1500, result_img.width
      assert_equal 1200, result_img.height
    end

    assert_equal 0, read_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count
    assert_equal files_before + 2, storage_file_count
  ensure
    tiff_file&.close!
  end

  test "Resque JSON serialization round-trip for ActiveJob arguments" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    clear_enqueued_jobs

    post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
      leaf: { title: "Resque Test" },
      picture: { image: fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp") }
    }
    assert_response :success
    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    blob = leaf.picture.image.blob

    # Manually drain queue with full JSON round-trip (exactly like Resque)
    bg_transforms = count_transforms do
      while enqueued_jobs.any?
        job_data = enqueued_jobs.shift
        json_roundtripped = JSON.parse(JSON.generate(job_data))
        job_class = json_roundtripped["job"].constantize
        args = ActiveJob::Arguments.deserialize(json_roundtripped["args"])
        job_class.perform_now(*args)
      end
    end

    assert_equal 1, bg_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count

    read_transforms = count_transforms do
      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]
      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
    end

    assert_equal 0, read_transforms
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.reload.count
  end

  test "non-variable image (BMP) does zero image processing and creates zero variants" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    files_before = storage_file_count

    transforms = count_transforms do
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        post book_pictures_path(book, format: :turbo_stream), params: {
          leaf: { title: "BMP" },
          picture: { image: fixture_file_upload("pixel.bmp", "image/bmp") }
        }
        assert_response :success
      end

      leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
      get book_slug_path(book)
      assert_response :success
      img_src = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body).at_css("#leaf_#{leaf.id} .toc__thumbnail img")["src"]
      get img_src
      assert_response :redirect
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
    end

    leaf = Leaf.order(:id).last
    assert_equal 0, transforms
    assert_equal 0, leaf.picture.image.blob.variant_records.count
    assert_equal files_before + 1, storage_file_count
  end
end

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**

```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**

```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**

```ruby
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```
